C.5 Equivalences involving function-theoretic properties of ζ
C.5.a Speiser’s criterion. A. Speiser (Math Annahlen 110 (1934) 514-521) proved that
the Riemann Hypothesis is equivalent to the non-vanishing of the derivative ζ 0 (s) in the
left-half of the critical strip 0 < σ < 1/2. Levinson and Montgomery [MR 54 #5135] gave
an alternative, quantitative version of this result which led to Levinson’s [MR 58 #27837]
discovery of his method for counting zeros on the critical line. He then proceeded to prove
that at least 1/3 of the zeros of ζ(s) are on the critical line.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Divisibility is encoded in an explicit finite 0–1 matrix, whose determinant growth carries an RH-equivalent exponent. This creates a combinatorial finite-dimensional observable, distinct from the accompanying spectral estimates.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source defines A(n) by A(i,j)=1 when j=1 or i divides j and 0 otherwise. It states RH is equivalent to det A(n)=O(n^(1/2+ε)) for every ε>0, and separately reports eigenvalue multiplicities, dominant-eigenvalue estimates, bounds on nontrivial eigenvalues, and a possible unit-disc conjecture.
directed.conceptual_reading: The matrix packages the divisibility poset into linear algebra. Determinant growth aggregates all eigenvalues and encodes the delicate arithmetic cancellation, whereas spectral radius and individual-eigenvalue bounds expose different, generally weaker observables.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The Redheffer matrix is the bridge from divisibility incidence to determinant asymptotics; its spectrum provides auxiliary diagnostics but is not interchangeable with the determinant criterion.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The stated eigenvalue information does not establish the RH-equivalent determinant bound, and the unit-disc remark is explicitly only a possibility. A finite matrix calculation at fixed n cannot settle the asymptotic condition.
directed.uncertainty: High for several spectral asymptotics, whose radicals and comparison symbols are corrupted. The matrix definition and determinant exponent are recoverable but should still be scan-verified for exact use.

supported: The span explicitly defines the 0-1 divisibility matrix A(n) and states the RH-equivalent determinant bound O(n^(1/2+epsilon)) for every epsilon>0.
